question: Sentence-law fix. The per-gap local-model adjudicator for unpunctuated transcripts was found to be a rubber stamp (gemma3:27b called 19 of 19 Yahoo Finance gaps sentence ends, including 'the | Wolf', 'of | all', 'is | up'). It is removed: sentence_law.boundary now returns invalid for any gap in an unpunctuated stretch (fail closed), and the adj parameter is gone from boundary, edge_plan, write_lock_cut_table, gate_g16 and their callers. Punctuation now comes from the ASR: select_passages._whisper_transcribe keeps the verbatim decode's words and, only where the transcript is unpunctuated, runs pipeline/punctuation.ensure, which decodes the same audio again with a neutral punctuated initial_prompt and copies trailing punctuation onto verbatim words in difflib equal blocks only (word keys asserted unchanged). Verify from the diff: (1) no path lets a gap without terminal punctuation become a sentence boundary; (2) transfer can never change, add or drop a word, and never puts a mark on a word the two decodes disagree on; (3) cached transcripts are re-punctuated or returned unchanged correctly; (4) no caller still passes the removed argument; (5) the must-fail tests (D3b's new reason, the rejected false ends, the reproduced fixture) are meaningful, not vacuous. Only state what you can verify; if uncertain, say so. (this chunk: pipeline/sentence_law.py)

rejected_findings.issue: External callers of boundary/edge_plan/write_lock_cut_table/gate_g16 that still pass the removed adj or context arguments (positionally or by keyword) will raise TypeError. This chunk only shows internal callers updated; the audit question (4) cannot be fully confirmed without seeing all call sites in other modules.
